name: Jeffrey Cheah
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sunway Group; Founder and Chancellor, Sunway University; Founder and Trustee, Jeffrey Cheah Foundation
profile: Malaysian tycoon who in 1974 left a job as an accountant at an auto assembly plant to buy a near-mined-out tin-mining company, then turned the land into Sunway City. Sunway now spans property, healthcare (Sunway Healthcare IPO'd in March 2026), construction, education and more; his children Sarena, Adrian and Evan work in the group.
interesting_fact: His Jeffrey Cheah Foundation, which owns Sunway University, is on track to award more than RM1 billion in scholarships and grants by 2026 - the largest such education foundation in Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Pusing, a small tin-mining town in Perak about 200 km north of Kuala Lumpur; seeing the scarred mining land there shaped his idea to rehabilitate the ex-mine that became Sunway City. He also co-chairs Mission 4.7, a UN SDSN education-for-sustainability initiative.
notes: Go through Sunway Group Corporate Communications (media form). Sunway warns of impersonation scams - only use official sunway.com.my channels. Sunway hosts annual media nights and is press-friendly; energy/infrastructure angle via Sunway's autonomous transport and electric aviation plans (Oct 2026).

name: Brad Garlinghouse
profile: Kansas-born executive (b. 1971) who held senior roles at @Home, Dialpad, Yahoo (SVP running Homepage, Flickr, Mail, Messenger) and AOL, then ran Hightail (ex-YouSendIt). Joined Ripple as COO in 2015 and became CEO around end-2016; his wealth comes from Ripple equity and XRP. He continues to lead Ripple's global payments, custody and RLUSD stablecoin push.
interesting_fact: As a Yahoo SVP in 2006 he wrote the internal 'Peanut Butter Manifesto' memo, warning Yahoo was spreading itself too thin like peanut butter; it leaked to the Wall Street Journal and became a Silicon Valley strategy classic.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his interest in technology began growing up in Kansas when his dad brought home a Tandy TRS-80 computer.
notes: Very media-accessible, active on X (@bgarlinghouse) and frequent podcast guest. Best route is Ripple's press team form. Avoid the long SEC-litigation saga as a hook.

name: Nadir Godrej
current_role: Chairperson, Godrej Industries Group (Godrej Industries, Godrej Consumer Products, Godrej Properties, Godrej Agrovet)
profile: Mumbai industrialist (b. 1951), younger brother of Adi Godrej, trained as a chemical engineer (MIT, Stanford) with a Harvard MBA, who joined the family business four-plus decades ago. After the 2024 family split he chairs the Godrej Industries Group - four listed companies with ~$6.1bn revenue spanning consumer goods, chemicals, real estate and agri.
interesting_fact: A published poet, he often delivers business speeches entirely in verse; his first collection, 'Life and Other Poems', appeared in 1992 and he has done joint poetry readings with novelist Vikram Seth.
deep_cut_fact: He started at IIT Bombay but transferred after one year to MIT for chemical engineering; he speaks six languages including Russian and French, is known for a love of mathematics, and is a Chevalier of France's Legion of Honour.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: 'Business and Poetry with Nadir Godrej' on AND is the Future podcast

notes: Approachable and has done podcasts before (sustainability angle; Godrej is a WBCSD member). A poetic hook in an outreach note would land well. Route via Godrej Industries media desk.
